## init
1. Maintain a low threshold for generating ideas and starting projects. 
2. Prioritize viability, functionality, and beauty over perfection. 
3. Suspend any evaluation or criticism until you produce a Version 1 or MVP. 

## continue 
1. Immediately begin to iteratively refine your project. Iterate often and fast. 
	- Establish a grounded routine (time, place, resources, task) for this.
2. Establish an explicit tracker for each project. 
3. Establish an explicit version history for your project. 
4. Solicit feedback from those who will encourage and constructively criticize. 
5. Review literature and reflect on the project's soundness and novelty. 

## conclude 
Decide on a project fate: mutation, archival, handover.
1. mutation: decide on mutation type (reduction, amplification, translocation) 
2. archival: decide on storage type (short-term for revisal/maintenance, long-term)
3. handover: Establish any necessary handover documents.

## meta 
1. When in doubt, embrace strong "as if"'s. e.g. Write this project design theory as if you were writing the constitution of a new country. e.g. Create Gantt charts as if you were programming a video game or designing a website. Write this project design theory as if you were writing code for a game.
2. You can learn from anything and anyone! There's no shame in borrowing inspiration from anyone and anything you see that you like.
